career_ladder.note: Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) Force, a premier Central Armed Police Force under the Ministry of Home Affairs, guards the high-altitude Indo-China border from Ladakh to Arunachal Pradesh. The Telecommunication cadre manages tactical wireless networks, satellite communications, and IT infrastructure. Sub-Inspectors and Head Constables advance through subordinate officer ranks to Group 'A' Gazetted combatised leadership.

exam_scheme.note: Selection is conducted in three phases: Phase-I comprises the Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and Physical Standard Test (PST) (qualifying nature); Phase-II comprises the Written Examination (100 multiple choice questions, 100 marks, 120 minutes) covering general aptitude and 50% technical/domain knowledge; Phase-III comprises Original Document Verification, Detailed Medical Examination (DME), and Review Medical Examination (RME).

financial_package.pay_source_label: ITBP — Recruitment Notice 2024, Pay Scale for Sub-Inspector (Telecom) Level 6
financial_package.estimate_note: Calculated at Level 6 entry basic pay (₹35,400) for Sub-Inspector (Telecom) with 58% DA (₹20,532), Ration Money Allowance (RMA, ₹3,900/mo), Transport Allowance, and Special High Altitude / Difficult Area Allowance (₹10,500 to ₹17,300/mo when deployed at forward Himalayan border posts). For Head Constable (Telecom) recruits at Level 4 (₹25,500 basic), initial monthly gross salary ranges from ₹48,000 to ₹67,000 with in-hand earnings between ₹42,000 and ₹59,000.
official_perks: Special High Altitude Allowance / Border Outpost Allowance (₹10,500 to ₹17,300/month at Himalayan forward posts)
Ration Money Allowance (RMA) / Free Government Messing (approx. ₹3,900/month)
Free medical treatment in ITBP and Central Armed Police Forces Composite Hospitals
Subsidized Central Police Canteen (CPC) purchasing privileges across India
Defined contribution retirement benefits under National Pension System (NPS)

competition_benchmarks.note: ITBP recruits technical personnel for high-altitude communications and border surveillance networks. In the 2024 recruitment cycle, 526 vacancies were notified across the Telecommunication cadre (17 Sub-Inspectors, 383 Head Constables, and 126 Constables). In the 2022 recruitment drive, 293 vacancies (126 Head Constables and 167 Constables) were advertised.
